title: Total fractions of a reduced Noetherian ring after prime localization
statement: Let $A$ be a reduced commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where reduced means that $a^n=0$ with $n\geq1$ implies $a=0$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal, put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For a commutative ring $D$, let $Q(D)=T_D^{-1}D$, where $T_D$ is the multiplicative set of non-zero-divisors (elements $t$ such that $td=0$ implies $d=0$); localizations are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let $S^{-1}Q(A)$ mean localization at the image of $S$ under $A\to Q(A)$. There is a canonical isomorphism of $R$-algebras $$S^{-1}Q(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(R).$$ It commutes with the maps from $R$: for $a\in A$ and $s\notin\mathfrak p$, the element $(a/1)/(s/1)$ maps to the image of $a/s\in R$. No assumption that $A$ is a domain is made.

source.place: Tag 02LX, label lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points. Agent-formulated prime-localization consequence of the finite product description; its complete deduction is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Put $T=T_A$ and $E=S^{-1}Q(A)$. For $t\in T$, if $(t/1)(a/s)=0$ in $R$, then $uta=0$ for some $u\in S$; cancellation of $t$ gives $ua=0$, hence $a/s=0$. Thus the image of $T$ consists of nonzerodivisors of $R$. The fraction rule defines $j:R\to E$ by $j(a/s)=(a/1)/(s/1)$: a relation $u(as^{\prime}-a^{\prime}s)=0$ remains a relation after mapping to $Q(A)$ and then inverting $S$. If $j(a/s)=0$, some $u\in S$ has $ua/1=0$ in $Q(A)$, hence $tua=0$ for some $t\in T$. Cancel $t$ to obtain $ua=0$, so $a/s=0$. Therefore $j$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00CO, label definition-localization: fraction equality and arithmetic; agent deduction from Tag 02LX, label lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points.

proof.text: Every element of $E$ has the form $x=(a/t)/(s/1)$ with $a\in A$, $t\in T$, $s\in S$. The element $j(t/1)$ is a unit, with inverse $(1/t)/1$, and fraction multiplication gives $$x=j(a/s)j(t/1)^{-1}.$$ In particular every element of $E$ is a fraction of an element of $R$ by the image of an element of $T$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, label definition-localization: fraction equality and arithmetic; agent deduction from Tag 02LX, label lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] to the reduced Noetherian ring $A$. It identifies $Q(A)$ with a finite product of fields $\prod_i A_{\mathfrak q_i}$. For $q\in Q(A)$ write its coordinates as $q_i$ and choose $v$ with coordinate $0$ if $q_i=0$, and $q_i^{-1}$ otherwise. In every coordinate $q_i^2v_i=q_i$, so $q^2v=q$. For $x=q/(s/1)\in E$, put $y=(s/1)v/1\in E$. Fraction multiplication gives $$x^2y=x.$$ This calculation includes zero coordinates; it makes no assumption that $A$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 02LX, label lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points, with Tags 00EU and 00EW as packaged in the cited reduced-Noetherian total-fractions node; coordinatewise reciprocal calculation by the agent.

proof.text: Let $r\in R$ be a nonzerodivisor and suppose $j(r)x=0$ in $E$. Write $x=j(b)j(t/1)^{-1}$ as in Step 2, with $b\in R$ and $t\in T$. Multiplication by the unit $j(t/1)$ gives $j(rb)=0$. Injectivity of $j$ gives $rb=0$ in $R$; regularity of $r$ gives $b=0$, hence $x=0$. Thus $j(r)$ is a nonzerodivisor of $E$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, label definition-localization: fraction equality and arithmetic; agent deduction from Tag 02LX, label lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points.

proof.text: For $r\in T_R$, apply Step 3 to $z=j(r)$ and obtain $y\in E$ with $z^2y=z$. Then $z(zy-1)=0$, and Step 4 gives $zy=1$. Thus every $j(r)$ with $r\in T_R$ is a unit in $E$. Define $F:Q(R)\to E$ by $F(b/r)=j(b)j(r)^{-1}$. It respects the fraction relation: if $w(br^{\prime}-b^{\prime}r)=0$ with $w\in T_R$, the image of $w$ is a unit, so $j(b)j(r^{\prime})=j(b^{\prime})j(r)$; multiplying by the denominator inverses proves equality of the images. The sum and product formulas show that $F$ is a unital ring map extending $j$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, label definition-localization: fraction equality and arithmetic; agent deduction from Tag 02LX, label lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points.

proof.text: Conversely send $a/t\in Q(A)$ to $(a/1)(t/1)^{-1}\in Q(R)$; Step 1 makes its denominator invertible. This is a ring map by the same fraction-relation calculation as in Step 5. Its image of each $s\in S$ is already a unit, since $s/1$ is a unit in $R$. It therefore defines $G:E\to Q(R)$ with $$G((a/t)/(s/1))=(a/s)(t/1)^{-1}.$$ In particular $G(j(b))=b$ for $b\in R$. Hence $GF(b/r)=b/r$. For $x=j(b)j(t/1)^{-1}$ as in Step 2, $FG(x)=j(b)j(t/1)^{-1}=x$. Thus $G$ is the desired isomorphism, inverse to $F$. Both maps respect the specified $R$-structures, and the displayed formula with $t=1$ gives precisely the required image of $(a/1)/(s/1)$.
